newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombians strip Britons' yacht for more cocaine.
newsitem.headline: Colombians strip Britons' yacht for more cocaine.

text.p: Police in a Colombian port on Wednesday began dismantling a luxury yacht owned by three British citizens looking for more cocaine on a ship that has already yielded $4.5 million worth of the drug.
Two searches of the vessel have so far turned up more than 750 pounds (340 kg) of cocaine. The three Britons were arrested in the port of Barranquilla on Dec. 13 and are being held in jail.

"We think there is a considerable quantity of cocaine still hidden on board, much more than has been found already," Armando Armenta, regional head of the state security service DAS, said. He said agents from the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration were assisting Colombian police.

The yacht owners -- Michael Hayne, 50, of Egham, Surrey, his son Stephen Alan Hayne, 27, of Ashford, Kent, and David Maurice Shaw, 49, of Oldham, Lancashire -- face up to 24 years in prison if convicted on drug chrages.
Shortly after their arrest Michael Hayne told Reuters from jail the arrests were a "huge mix-up".
The yacht, the Perla Del Mar, was purchased in Colombia for $500,000 and the Britons had planned to sail it to the Netherlands, Armenta said.
